title: REA server enables AI agents to reverse engineer software
key_facts: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) is a new open-source MCP server and command-line tool that lets programming agents disassemble software without source code.
It can point agents such as Claude Code or Codex at native binaries, Electron apps, .NET assemblies, Android APKs, websites or saved network captures.
It returns pseudocode, module graphs, request logs and evidence explaining how a function works.
TechGig reports the morluto/rea GitHub repository gained over 115,000 stars and 25,000 forks within a week and led GitHub Trending for five days between 6 and 12 Oct.
REA runs locally; deep native analysis needs engines such as Hopper, Ghidra 12.1 with JDK 21 or higher, or IDA.
For API teams it reads HAR or mitmproxy captures offline and builds an inferred API inventory.
quote_evidence: REA, or Reverse Engineer Anything, functions as an open-source MCP server and command-line interface, providing programming agents with tools to disassemble software without its source code.
The morluto/rea repository garnered over 115,000 stars and 25,000 forks on GitHub within a week in October
REA operates locally, with agents calling its tools to inspect targets using appropriate engines
why_it_matters_hint: A very popular open tool now lets AI agents take apart software, useful for security and API work but also open to misuse.
notes: One outlet; the star count is TechGig's figure and was not checked against GitHub. Other outlets (HackerNoon, SitePoint, Pasquale Pillitteri) carried the tool 13-14 Oct. Tool appeared before the article date.
